images.subject: Mill Creek's concrete flood-control channel beside N. 6th Avenue, downtown Walla Walla (2014)
images.author: Joe Mabel
images.attribution: Photo: Joe Mabel, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Mill Creek in its concrete flood channel beside N. 6th Avenue downtown. The channel is a federal flood-control project (U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, paved 1948), which is why the draft treats Mill Creek differently from the smaller creeks.
images.alt: A curved concrete flood channel with a thin stream of water at the bottom, trees and a substation fence above the walls.

images.subject: Mill Creek Channel at high water, Walla Walla, 7 February 2020 (U.S. Army Corps of Engineers)
images.author: Joseph Saxon, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Northwestern Division
images.attribution: Photo: Joseph Saxon, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (public domain), via DVIDS
images.caption: Mill Creek running high in the Corps-built flood channel, February 2020. Photo: Joseph Saxon, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (public domain).
images.alt: Brown floodwater racing through a creek channel past bare trees and an eroded gravel bank under a grey sky.

images.subject: Lower Mill Creek near Old Highway 12, west of College Place, looking downstream (April 2026)
images.author: Generalissima
images.attribution: Photo: Generalissima, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Mill Creek below town, near Old Highway 12 west of College Place, where it runs free of the concrete channel. This reach is outside the city limits.
images.alt: A wide, shallow creek with a gravel bar and a fallen log, lined by leafy trees under a bluff.

images.subject: Bandstand in Pioneer Park, Walla Walla (2013)
images.author: Robert Ashworth
images.attribution: Photo: Robert Ashworth, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: The bandstand in Pioneer Park. Garrison Creek runs through the park, a few blocks from the Home Avenue example.
images.alt: A white octagonal bandstand with a copper roof under large old trees in a park.

images.subject: Lakum Duckum, the pond on College Creek at Whitman College (2009)
images.author: PSB (Wikimedia Commons user)
images.attribution: Photo: PSB, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Lakum Duckum, the pond on College Creek at Whitman College. Small creeks like this one thread through the whole east side of town.
images.alt: A still campus pond with lily pads, a small waterfall and willows reflected in the water.

images.subject: Summer lawn and mature trees on the Whitman College campus (2004)
images.author: Suzanne Shaw
images.attribution: Photo: Suzanne Shaw, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr / Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Old shade trees on the Whitman College campus.
images.alt: A sunlit lawn with a wooden bench under tall, spreading trees.

images.subject: Wheat field and the Walla Walla water tower at dusk (June 2018)
images.author: Jason W Lacey
images.attribution: Photo: Jason W Lacey, CC0, via Flickr / Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Wheat at the edge of town, with the Walla Walla water tower behind.
images.alt: Golden wheat in the foreground, a round white water tower painted with the word Walla Walla, and a pink dusk sky.

images.subject: Main Street, downtown Walla Walla, with the Dacres Hotel building (July 2021)
images.author: Ken Lund
images.attribution: Photo: Ken Lund, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Flickr / Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Main Street downtown.
images.alt: A sunny downtown street with a three-storey historic hotel building, street trees and parked cars.

images.subject: East Main Street at South First Avenue, Walla Walla Downtown Historic District (September 2021)
images.author: Jon Roanhaus
images.attribution: Photo: Jon Roanhaus, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

images.subject: The Blue Mountains from the Walla Walla Valley (February 2011)
images.author: Agne27
images.attribution: Photo: Agne27, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: The Blue Mountains from farmland in the Walla Walla Valley. Most of the valley's creeks begin up there.
images.alt: A dark plowed field in the foreground and snow-covered mountains under a sky of broken cloud.

images.subject: Kirkman House Museum, N. Colville Street, under mature street trees (2012)
images.author: Phbludwig
images.attribution: Photo: Phbludwig, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: The Kirkman House Museum on North Colville Street, one of the older residential blocks in town. (A public museum, shown as a street scene; it is not an example of an affected lot.)
images.alt: A two-storey brick Italianate house with white trim and a lawn, framed by large old trees.

images.subject: "Scene on the Yellow Hawk Creek", Walla Walla, 1906 postcard (Brück & Sohn)
images.author: Brück & Sohn Kunstverlag, Meissen (1906 postcard)
images.license: CC0 1.0 (publisher's archive release; also public domain by age)
images.attribution: 1906 postcard: Brück & Sohn Kunstverlag, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Yellowhawk Creek on a 1906 postcard, already fitted with a small dam. The city's creeks have been worked, moved and built beside for well over a century.
images.alt: A sepia 1906 postcard of a creek pouring over a low wooden dam between leafy trees.

images.subject: "Scene on Mill Creek", Walla Walla, 1906 postcard (Brück & Sohn)
images.author: Brück & Sohn Kunstverlag, Meissen (1906 postcard)
images.license: CC0 1.0 (publisher's archive release; also public domain by age)
images.attribution: 1906 postcard: Brück & Sohn Kunstverlag, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Mill Creek on a 1906 postcard, four decades before it was paved into a flood channel.
images.alt: A sepia 1906 postcard of a shallow, tree-lined creek with a gravel bed.
